sites.does: fires a high-signal materiality feature when a statement names a person or entity
sites.consequence: was scoring a statement naming only the author as an attribution to an outside party, raising its materiality level and, through it, its flag register. The register filtered the feature out downstream at a5be4f0; FIXED at the producer here, so every consumer now sees the same answer

sites.does: marks Title-Case runs as verifiable anchors a source should corroborate
sites.consequence: none that is wrong. An anchor is a checkable thing, not an outside party, and the author's own name in a statement is legitimately checkable
sites.resolverAccess: yes, but it should not use it

sites.does: rejects a stage 1 edit introducing a proper noun absent from the statement and sources
sites.probe: with resolver ok=true, without resolver ok=false
sites.consequence: was discarding correct directive edits that named the client. Fixed at 2528a32
sites.resolverAccess: yes, threaded through runStage1 as authoringOrganisation

sites.does: rejects a no-span edit that DELETES a named entity the finding does not name
sites.probe: dropping the author's name is rejected=true (removed without being flagged: Halden Group)
sites.consequence: none that is wrong. This guard protects against LOSING a name, and losing who acted is a real defect whether the actor is the author or anyone else
sites.resolverAccess: yes, but it should not use it

sites.does: decides whether a flagged element names an outside party, driving the LOUD register
sites.consequence: was pushing the author's own statements to LOUD. Fixed at a5be4f0

sites.does: extracts the checkable particulars in a sentence; the count decides whether removing a clause leaves a remnant worth keeping
sites.probe: author-only [], third-party ["Meridian Capital"], mixed ["Meridian Capital Partners V"]
sites.consequence: was counting the author's own name as a particular an outside source must support, so a sentence about the author's own actions looked more checkable than it is. It already filtered first-person pronouns, which is the same actor by another name. FIXED here

sites.does: takes the FIRST Title-Case run in the statement as the entity, and requires the source excerpt to contain it before the proposition can be confirmed
sites.probe: entity-led confirmed=true, author-led confirmed=true, author-only confirmed=false
sites.consequence: a supported statement that OPENS with the author's name could never be confirmed, because no external source mentions the client. A false negative on SUPPORT, the most consequential of the confusions found. FIXED here; where the author is the only name there is still no external anchor and the proposition stays unconfirmed

sites.does: decides whether a statement attributes an act to the author rather than a third party
sites.consequence: this site exists to make the distinction; it is the reference implementation
